revisions.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. The subject MUST be methane CH4: exactly ONE larger central teal carbon sphere and FOUR smaller hydrogen spheres. Think of an actual physical 3D methane ball-and-stick model with 109.47-degree H-C-H angles. Use an oblique camera perspective that makes depth unmistakable: ONE hydrogen is the upper apex, the OTHER THREE form a triangular base below the carbon; the nearest basal hydrogen projects toward the viewer with a foreshortened bond and slightly overlaps the carbon/bond in perspective, while the other two basal hydrogens recede to the left and right, with their bond roots partly occluded by the carbon sphere. This near-versus-far arrangement must clearly show three-dimensional tetrahedral coordination, not four equally visible coplanar arms. All four C-H bond axes must belong to the same genuine tetrahedral geometry. Do not connect hydrogens to each other and do not draw the tetrahedron's edges. Make the carbon sphere from smooth interlocking jigsaw segments with a few clear curved puzzle seams, and make the bond parts interlock. The upper apex hydrogen with a short bond fragment is warm pale peach and floats only a small distance along its correct bond axis above the matching open puzzle connector; the three basal hydrogens are pale mint. Keep this as methane being assembled, with all five atom spheres in frame and generous transparent margins. No ethane, no second carbon, no rectangular puzzle board, no flat X arrangement, no right-angle bond layout, no text, symbols, letters, numbers, pedestal, scene, glow, haze, shadow backdrop or watermark.
